subject.title: fix(cron): keep isolated run status ok when delivery fails

question: Should successful isolated cron execution with post-run delivery failure be recorded as `status=ok` plus `deliveryStatus=not-delivered`, or should OpenClaw preserve error semantics or introduce a first-class warning status before landing this behavior?
rationale: The implementation is narrow and tested, but the choice changes persisted run status, backoff, failure alerts, and external operator semantics for undelivered successful runs.

options.title: Land focused decoupling
options.body: Accept `status=ok` for successful execution and require delivery-aware consumers to use `deliveryStatus`, `lastDeliveryError`, and diagnostics for undelivered runs.

options.title: Prefer warning status
options.body: Pause this PR and pursue the broader `warning` status model after resolving protocol, UI, CLI, plugin, and client compatibility.

options.title: Keep error semantics
options.body: Reject this direction for now so post-run delivery failures continue to drive `status=error`, backoff, and failure alerts.

recommendation.title: Land focused decoupling
recommendation.body: Accept `status=ok` for successful execution and require delivery-aware consumers to use `deliveryStatus`, `lastDeliveryError`, and diagnostics for undelivered runs.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across cron status, protocol, server, and docs surfaces, and the remaining blocker is product/API compatibility rather than a local code repair.
